summary: CCC-built 100-foot steel tower in Bankhead National Forest, Winston County, dated circa 1936-1938; fenced off, reached over private land; NHLR-registered 2016.

facts.design: 100-foot steel tower with 7 by 7 foot cab

access.note: The Register says the tower is fenced off. The access road crosses private property; the Register asks visitors to get the nearby landowner's permission.

events.note: Built by CCC workers between 1936 and 1938; the Register's build field reads circa 1936-1938

evidence.supports: built by CCC workers between 1936 and 1938
evidence.quote: Black Pond Lookout Tower was built by CCC workers between 1936 and 1938.

evidence.supports: design: 100-foot steel tower with 7 by 7 foot cab
evidence.quote: It is a 100' steel tower with 7'x7' cab.

evidence.supports: wood replaced in recent years, date not given
evidence.quote: All wood in the tower has been replaced in recent years.

evidence.supports: access road crosses private property; ask landowner for permission
evidence.quote: The access road to the tower crosses private property. Please ask the nearby landowner for permission.

evidence.supports: administered by the U.S. Forest Service
located in Bankhead National Forest, Winston County, Alabama
Bankhead National Forest and Winston County on the Forest Lookouts page
many Alabama towers are in poor shape, very unsafe and illegal to climb
evidence.quote: Many are looking worse for the wear, are very unsafe, and are illegal to climb.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's single year, 1936, is the start of the Register's circa 1936-1938 range and the CCC build period of 1936 to 1938, so it is not a firm date.

sources.title: Thomas Kaufmann: Keeping Alabama's historic lookout towers

notes_for_editor: One detailed Register entry (nominated by Andrew Zerb; photo credit Andrew Zerbe) and a thin Forest Lookouts page. No staffing, fire, restoration-date or current-status sources were found. A Forest Service Bankhead page read had no tower content. The 30.5 m height is the 100-foot tower height converted, not a cab-floor height. The record's built year of 1936 may be widened to the Register's circa 1936-1938 range.
